name: Molletes
summary: Toasted rolls spread with homemade refried pinto beans and melted cheese, topped with a quick tomato salsa.

ingredients.name: pinto beans, drained (keep a little liquid)
yellow onion, finely diced (half for the beans, half for salsa)
diced tomatoes, well drained, for salsa

instructions: Melt 2 tbsp butter in a pan and cook half the onion 4 minutes. Add the beans, cumin, and a splash of their liquid, and mash into a thick paste over low heat, about 5 minutes. Season with salt.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Spread the cut sides of the rolls with the rest of the butter and bake 5 minutes until lightly toasted.
Spread each half with refried beans and top with cheese.
Bake 6–8 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Mix the drained tomatoes with the rest of the onion and a pinch of salt, and spoon over the molletes.

substitutions.substitute: 8 corn tortillas, baked flat until crisp (as tostadas), with the same toppings
substitutions.costNote: $1.99 instead of $3.97, bringing the total to about $11.05

glutenFree.notes: The beans, cheese, and salsa are naturally gluten-free. The rolls are the only source of gluten.

budgetNotes: Substitution: dinner rolls replace bolillos, the crusty Mexican rolls. The texture changes: bolillos have a hard, crackly crust and chewy inside that stays crisp under the beans. Dinner rolls are softer and sweeter and go soft faster, so serve them straight from the oven. A split baguette is closer to the real thing.

Substitution: cheddar replaces queso fresco, which isn't reliably stocked at Ottawa chain stores. The taste changes: queso fresco is mild, milky and slightly salty, and crumbles without melting. Cheddar is sharper and melts into strings. If you find queso fresco or feta, crumble it on at the end instead.
Homemade refried beans from canned pintos cost less than half the price of canned refried beans ($3.87 a can for La Costeña).
A good breakfast or late-night meal. Most of it can be made ahead.
